name: adaptive-nav
title: Adaptive nav
description: One list of destinations that is a bottom bar on a phone, a rail on a tablet and a sidebar on a desktop, chosen by its own width, with focus kept on the same item.
docs: Pass items ({ id, label, icon, href, badge, badgeLabel, group }), current (an id) and the page as children. The component measures its own width, not the window's, and follows the compact, medium and expanded window classes: below breakpoints.medium (600) it is a bar along the bottom, from there to breakpoints.expanded (840) a rail of icons with tooltips, and above that a sidebar with the groups as headings. Only one shape is in the page at a time, the current item carries aria-current in all of them, and when the shape changes focus goes to the same item in the new one. The bar shows the first four items and More, which opens a sheet inside the component with the rest, the header and the footer; five items and no header or footer fit without it. header and footer are the brand and the account: they fill the top and bottom of the sidebar and rail, and read the shape with useAdaptiveNavForm(), or with group-data-[form=rail]/adaptive-nav: classes. An item with an href is a link and an item without is a button; onNavigate(item, event) runs on a plain click, and a link is routed by you only when you call event.preventDefault(), so open-in-new-tab keeps working. A badge is a count or a short word, with badgeLabel to say what it counts. initialForm is the shape drawn on the server before the width is known. labels translates every word.
